ground_truth_question: What security permissions and access controls are required for internal OSS tools per the checklist?
ground_truth_answer: Internal OSS tools must comply with BCG Information Security best practices and access restrictions, meaning teams should confirm appropriate permissioning and controls are consistently in place.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Ensure permissions comply with BCG Information Security best practices and access restrictions.

ground_truth_question: What dependency and security evaluation should engineers perform for internal OSS use?
ground_truth_answer: Engineers must understand all code, library, API, and data dependencies associated with the OSS and evaluate them for security compliance as part of the internal‑use checklist.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Understand any code, library, API, data dependencies of the OSS and evaluate for security compliance.

policy_content_file_name: Open-Source Software Usage and AI Standard-v.1.1.pdf
ground_truth_question: What maintenance planning does the internal‑use checklist require?
ground_truth_answer: Teams must develop a maintenance plan, including a schedule, and identify an owner responsible for upkeep to ensure the OSS component remains secure and supported over time.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Develop a maintain plan including a schedule and identify the owner.

ground_truth_question: What data‑handling constraint is emphasized for internal OSS tools in the checklist?
ground_truth_answer: The checklist reiterates that OSS‑based tools must not process PII or sensitive data, underscoring the data‑minimization and privacy requirements for internal use.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Ensure the OSS-based tool does not process PII or sensitive data.
policy_title: Open-Source Software Usage and AI Standard

ground_truth_question: What AI‑specific approvals are required for internal OSS tools according to the checklist?
ground_truth_answer: AI tools and models must be submitted to the Responsible AI Team and the OSS Management Team for approval prior to deployment. This ensures consistency with responsible AI and licensing controls before release.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
AI tools and models checks:
 o Submit tool to RAI (RAI@BCG.com) and OSS Management Team (OSSManagementTeam@BCG.com) for approval prior to deployment

ground_truth_question: How should teams prevent inadvertent disclosure of inputs or training data in internal AI tools?
ground_truth_answer: Teams must ensure the tool does not expose input or training data outside of BCG, protecting sensitive information and preventing leakage through logs, telemetry, or external integrations.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: o Ensure the tool does not expose input or training data outside of BCG.
policy_title: Open-Source Software Usage and AI Standard

policy_content_file_name: Open-Source Software Usage and AI Standard-v.1.1.pdf
ground_truth_question: What training‑data IP and web‑scraping requirements apply to internal AI tools?
ground_truth_answer: Training data must not be subject to IP protection and must not violate BCG’s web‑scraping policy. Teams should vet data sources and acquisition methods accordingly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: o Ensure training data is not subject to IP protection and does not violate BCG’s web scraping policy (available on Knowledge Navigator)

ground_truth_question: What documentation is required for internal AI models in the checklist?
ground_truth_answer: Teams must document the AI model and its training dataset, creating an auditable record of sources and preparation that supports governance, reproducibility, and model risk management.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: o Document AI model and training data set.

ground_truth_answer: Teams must check the client contracts to ensure there are no prohibitions on the use of client data with OSS tools and verify any disclosure or attribution requirements that may apply.

policy_content_file_name: Open-Source Software Usage and AI Standard-v.1.1.pdf
ground_truth_question: What steps are required to create a new BCG OSS project or to contribute to new BCG projects per the public‑contributions checklist?
ground_truth_answer: Contributors should reach out to the OSS Management Team, identify a desired OSS license, obtain an MDP sponsor, ensure permissions align with BCG security practices and access restrictions, understand dependencies and evaluate security compliance, develop a maintenance plan with an owner, ensure no release of BCG or client IP, and ensure no violation of client confidentiality obligations.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
For new contributions to BCG projects, or to create new BCG projects, reach out to the OSS Management Team at OSSManagementTeam@bcg.com 
 o Identify the license under which you would like to distribute the OSS.
 o Obtain an MDP sponsor for the project.
 o Ensure permissions comply with BCG Information Security best practices and access restrictions.
 o Understand any code, library, API, data dependencies of the OSS and evaluate for security compliance.
 o Develop a maintain plan including a schedule and identify an owner. 
 o Ensure the contribution will not release BCG or Client IP
 o Ensure the contribution does not violate client confidentiality obligations.

exact_excerpt_from_policy:
AI tools and models checks:
 o Submit tool to RAI (RAI@BCG.com) and OSS Management Team (OSSManagementTeam@BCG.com) for approval prior to deployment
 o Ensure training data is not subject to IP protection and does not violate BCG’s web scraping policy (available on Knowledge Navigator)
 o Document AI model and training data set.
 o Ensure the contribution does not rely on or make calls to foundational models not approved by BCG.
